4. Right-click the browser tab at the top. What you should see: Its tab menu appears.

5. If Unmute site appears, click it. What you should see: Chrome allows audio from that site.

Check whether the fix worked

The video produces sound.

If it still does not work

If every app is silent, use the Windows sound lessons. If only this video fails, test another video on the same site.

More browser problems

Lesson 57 A PDF opens in Chrome when you wanted to save it

What the problem means

Chrome’s PDF viewer can display a file without placing a saved copy where you expect.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open the PDF link from a trusted source. What you should see: The document appears in Chrome.

2. Move your mouse near the top of the PDF viewer. What you should see: Its toolbar becomes visible.

3. Click the Download icon, usually a downward arrow. What you should see: A Save dialog appears or the file downloads.

4. If asked, select Downloads or Documents and click Save. What you should see: The file is stored in that folder.

5. Press Ctrl and J, then click Show in folder beside the PDF. What you should see: You can locate the saved copy.

Check whether the fix worked

A local PDF file is visible in the intended folder.

If it still does not work

If no download is allowed, the website may restrict it. Do not confuse a link with a downloaded file.

More browser problems

Lesson 58 A webpage form lost your typed information

What the problem means

Unsaved form data may disappear when a page reloads or a session expires.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Stay on the page and avoid repeated reloads. What you should see: You preserve whatever remains.

2. Check whether the site saved a draft or shows a Resume option. What you should see: A saved version may be available.

3. If the browser Back button can safely return to the form, click it once. What you should see: Some forms retain the previous entries.

4. For your next attempt, write long answers in a document first and save them. What you should see: You have a recoverable copy.

5. Copy the saved answer into the form and submit before the session expires. What you should see: You reduce the chance of losing it again.

Check whether the fix worked

You find a saved draft or complete a new form using saved text.

If it still does not work

There is no guaranteed recovery for an unsaved form. For payment forms, check transaction status before submitting again.

More browser problems

Lesson 59 Chrome saved the wrong password

What the problem means

An old saved password can fill a form even after the account password changes.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open the official sign-in page. What you should see: You confirm the correct site.

2. Click the password box and select its existing contents. What you should see: The old autofilled password is highlighted.

3. Type the current password and sign in. What you should see: You test the actual current password.

4. If Chrome offers to update the saved password, read the site and username shown. What you should see: You can confirm the correct saved entry.

5. Click Update only for that matching entry. What you should see: Chrome replaces the saved password.

Check whether the fix worked

The next sign-in fills the correct password.

If it still does not work

If no update prompt appears, open Chrome’s Google Password Manager and edit only the matching site entry.

More browser problems

Lesson 60 A page says your connection is not private

What the problem means

A certificate warning may come from the site, a wrong clock, or a network sign-in page.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Stop on the warning page without entering a password. What you should see: You avoid sending private details through a questionable connection.

2. Read the address and error code and write them down. What you should see: You identify the site and warning.

3. Check the Windows date and time against your phone. What you should see: You can spot an incorrect clock.

4. If wrong, use Lesson 50 to correct the clock, then reload the site. What you should see: You can test whether time caused the warning.

5. If using public Wi-Fi, open its legitimate network sign-in page if provided. What you should see: You can finish required network access.

Check whether the fix worked

The warning clears after a legitimate correction, or you have the exact error to report.

If it still does not work

If it persists only on one site, contact that site or retry later. Do not click through the warning just to enter credentials.

Display and everyday hardware

Lesson 61 Everything on the screen is too small

What the problem means

Windows display scale can make app text and controls hard to read.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click the Windows Start button on the taskbar. What you should see: The Start menu opens.

2. Click Settings. If it is not visible, type Settings and click the Settings app in the results. What you should see: The Windows Settings window opens.

3. Click System. What you should see: The System settings appear.

4. Click Display. What you should see: The Display settings appear.

5. Find Scale under Scale and layout. What you should see: A scale percentage appears.

6. Record the current percentage. What you should see: You can restore it if needed.

7. Choose the recommended value or the next larger standard value. What you should see: Apps become larger.

8. Read a familiar window and check that controls still fit. What you should see: You can judge readability.

Check whether the fix worked

Text and controls are comfortable and fit on screen.

If it still does not work

If only one webpage is small, use browser zoom instead. Avoid custom scaling before trying standard values.

Display and everyday hardware

Lesson 62 The screen is too dim

What the problem means

Brightness or an external monitor’s controls may be set too low.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click the Windows Start button on the taskbar. What you should see: The Start menu opens.

2. Click Settings. If it is not visible, type Settings and click the Settings app in the results. What you should see: The Windows Settings window opens.

3. Click System. What you should see: The System settings appear.

4. Click Display. What you should see: The Display settings appear.

5. Look for the Brightness slider. What you should see: A laptop with adjustable built-in brightness usually shows it.

6. Move the slider a little to the right. What you should see: The screen becomes brighter.

7. If no slider exists, use the physical menu buttons on your external monitor. What you should see: The monitor’s own controls open.

8. Find Brightness in the monitor menu and increase it moderately. What you should see: The external display brightens.

Check whether the fix worked

You can read the display clearly.

If it still does not work

If brightness will not change, note the monitor model and whether the problem started after an update.

Display and everyday hardware

Lesson 63 The picture looks stretched or blurry

What the problem means

The display may be using a resolution that does not match its panel.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click the Windows Start button on the taskbar. What you should see: The Start menu opens.

2. Click Settings. If it is not visible, type Settings and click the Settings app in the results. What you should see: The Windows Settings window opens.

3. Click System. What you should see: The System settings appear.

4. Click Display. What you should see: The Display settings appear.

5. If more than one screen is shown, click the affected screen’s rectangle. What you should see: You select the display to adjust.

6. Find Display resolution and record its current value. What you should see: You have the original setting.

7. Choose the option marked Recommended. What you should see: Windows previews that resolution.

8. If the picture is clear, click Keep changes. If unusable, wait for Windows to revert. What you should see: The choice is saved or safely restored.

Check whether the fix worked

The picture is clear and has normal proportions.

If it still does not work

If a monitor is connected through an adapter, record that adapter and the available resolutions.

Display and everyday hardware

Lesson 64 A second monitor shows no picture

What the problem means

The screen may have the wrong input, a loose cable, or the wrong projection mode.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Check that the second monitor is powered on. What you should see: Its power indicator is lit.

2. Check both ends of the display cable. What you should see: The cable is seated in the PC and monitor.

3. Use the monitor’s input button to select the port carrying that cable, such as HDMI. What you should see: The monitor listens to the correct connection.

4. Hold the Windows key and press P. What you should see: Projection options appear.

5. Choose Extend or Duplicate. What you should see: Windows sends a picture to the second screen.

Check whether the fix worked

The second screen shows the desktop.

If it still does not work

If absent, open Display settings and use Detect if offered. Test a known working cable before replacing hardware.

Display and everyday hardware

Lesson 65 The desktop appears on the wrong monitor

What the problem means

Windows may have chosen the wrong main display.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click the Windows Start button on the taskbar. What you should see: The Start menu opens.

2. Click Settings. If it is not visible, type Settings and click the Settings app in the results. What you should see: The Windows Settings window opens.

3. Click System. What you should see: The System settings appear.

4. Click Display. What you should see: The Display settings appear.

5. Click Identify. What you should see: A number appears on each screen.

6. Click the rectangle matching the screen you want as primary. What you should see: That display is selected.

7. Expand Multiple displays if needed. What you should see: Additional display options appear.

8. Select Make this my main display. What you should see: Windows moves primary desktop functions to that screen.

Check whether the fix worked

The intended monitor acts as the main screen.

If it still does not work

If only one monitor is detected, fix its connection before changing main display settings.

Display and everyday hardware

Lesson 66 The screen is sideways

What the problem means

The display orientation may have changed.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click the Windows Start button on the taskbar. What you should see: The Start menu opens.

2. Click Settings. If it is not visible, type Settings and click the Settings app in the results. What you should see: The Windows Settings window opens.

3. Click System. What you should see: The System settings appear.

4. Click Display. What you should see: The Display settings appear.

5. Select the affected display if there are several. What you should see: You choose the correct screen.

6. Find Display orientation. What you should see: Its current orientation appears.

7. Choose Landscape for a standard upright monitor. What you should see: The picture rotates.

8. Click Keep changes only if it looks correct. What you should see: The orientation is saved.

Check whether the fix worked

The screen is upright.

If it still does not work

For a tablet or intentionally rotated monitor, use the orientation matching its physical position.

Display and everyday hardware

Lesson 67 The mouse stops responding

What the problem means

A wireless battery, receiver, or cable problem can prevent movement.

Fix it one step at a time

1. If wireless, turn the mouse off and back on with its own switch. What you should see: Its indicator may light.

2. Replace or recharge its battery if low. What you should see: The mouse has power.

3. If it uses a USB receiver, remove and reconnect that receiver directly to the PC. What you should see: The receiver connection restarts.

4. If wired, reconnect the USB cable or try another PC port. What you should see: You test the wired connection.

5. Move the mouse on a plain surface and test clicking. What you should see: You can check whether it responds.

Check whether the fix worked

The pointer moves and clicks work.

If it still does not work

For Bluetooth mice, check Bluetooth connection. If another mouse works in the same port, the original mouse may need service.

Display and everyday hardware

Lesson 68 The laptop touchpad does not move the pointer

What the problem means

The touchpad may have been disabled by a key or Windows setting.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click the Windows Start button on the taskbar. What you should see: The Start menu opens.

2. Click Settings. If it is not visible, type Settings and click the Settings app in the results. What you should see: The Windows Settings window opens.

3. Click Bluetooth & devices. What you should see: The Bluetooth & devices settings appear.

4. Click Touchpad. What you should see: The Touchpad settings appear.

5. Read the main Touchpad switch. What you should see: You can see whether it is enabled.

6. If off, switch it on. What you should see: Touchpad input is enabled.

7. Move one finger across the touchpad. What you should see: The pointer should move.

8. If a mouse is attached, unplug it briefly and test again. What you should see: You can check whether external-mouse behavior is involved.

Check whether the fix worked

The touchpad controls the pointer.

If it still does not work

If you cannot navigate without a pointer, connect a USB mouse. Some laptops also have a function key marked with a touchpad icon.

Display and everyday hardware

Lesson 69 The number keypad will not type numbers

What the problem means

Num Lock may be off, so keypad keys move the cursor instead.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click Start, type Notepad, and click the matching app in the results. What you should see: Notepad opens.

2. Click inside the blank document. What you should see: The text cursor appears.

3. Press Num Lock once on the keyboard’s numeric keypad. What you should see: Its mode changes; a light may turn on.

4. Type 1, 2, and 3 on the numeric keypad. What you should see: You can check whether digits appear.

5. If they still do not type, test the number row above the letters. What you should see: You can compare the keypad with the main keyboard.

Check whether the fix worked

The keypad types digits.

If it still does not work

Compact laptops may use a function-key combination. Check the keyboard’s labels rather than guessing random shortcuts.

Display and everyday hardware

Lesson 70 A USB accessory works poorly through a hub

What the problem means

An unpowered or faulty hub can cause a device to disconnect.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Save work and stop using the accessory before disconnecting it. What you should see: You avoid interrupting a file transfer.

2. Unplug the accessory from the USB hub. What you should see: It disconnects.

3. Plug it directly into a USB port on the computer. What you should see: Windows detects it directly.

4. Repeat its normal task, such as moving a mouse or testing a webcam. What you should see: You compare operation without the hub.

5. If direct use works, reconnect through another hub port if available. What you should see: You can isolate one bad hub port.

Check whether the fix worked

The device works directly or you identify that the hub causes the symptom.

If it still does not work

For drives, use safe removal before unplugging. A power-hungry accessory may need a powered hub specified by its manufacturer.

Word document problems

Lesson 71 Word will not let you edit a downloaded document

What the problem means

Protected View can intentionally open downloaded documents in a restricted mode.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open the document in desktop Word. What you should see: The document and any warning banner appear.

2. Read the banner at the top. What you should see: You identify Protected View rather than a password lock.

3. Confirm you expected this document and trust its source. What you should see: You can decide whether editing is appropriate.

4. If trusted, click Enable Editing on that banner. What you should see: Word allows editing.

5. Make a small intended edit and press Ctrl and S. What you should see: You can test saving.

Check whether the fix worked

The trusted file can be edited and saved.

If it still does not work

For an unknown file, keep Protected View on. A password-protected or unlicensed document needs a different solution.

Word document problems

Lesson 72 Word opens a document as read only

What the problem means

The file may lack editing permission or be locked by someone else.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Read the message or banner near the top of Word. What you should see: You identify the reason shown.

2. Click File in the upper left. What you should see: The file menu opens.

3. Click Save As, then Browse if available. What you should see: A save location dialog opens.

4. Choose Documents and give the copy a new name. What you should see: You avoid overwriting the original.

5. Click Save, then edit the new copy. What you should see: You can work on a file you control.

Check whether the fix worked

The separate copy can be edited without replacing the original.

If it still does not work

If the original belongs to a shared folder, ask its owner for edit access. Do not bypass someone else’s lock.

Word document problems

Lesson 73 Word changes disappeared after a crash

What the problem means

A recovery copy may exist, but unsaved work is not always recoverable.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open Word again. What you should see: A Document Recovery pane may appear.

2. If recovery files are listed, compare their names and timestamps. What you should see: You can choose the most relevant copy.

3. Open the likely copy and inspect the final paragraphs. What you should see: You check what was preserved.

4. Click File, then Save As. What you should see: You can save a recovered version separately.

5. Choose a clear new filename and click Save. What you should see: The recovery copy is preserved.

Check whether the fix worked

You saved the best available recovery copy.

If it still does not work

If no recovery pane appears, check File, Info, Manage Document, Recover Unsaved Documents if available. Future protection depends on saving regularly and recovery settings.

Word document problems

Lesson 74 Word has an unwanted blank page

What the problem means

Extra empty paragraphs or a manual page break can create a blank page.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Save a copy before changing page structure. What you should see: You can return to the original layout.

2. Click Home on Word’s ribbon. What you should see: Home controls appear.

3. Click the paragraph symbol, called Show or Hide. What you should see: Paragraph marks and manual breaks become visible.

4. Go to the blank page and identify empty paragraph marks or a labeled Page Break. What you should see: You can see what is occupying it.

5. Select only an unnecessary empty mark or manual Page Break and press Delete. What you should see: The extra space may disappear.

6. Check the preceding and following pages. What you should see: You confirm that real content was not removed.

Check whether the fix worked

The extra blank page disappears and nearby content remains intact.

If it still does not work

Do not casually delete a Section Break; it can change layout. A final paragraph after a table may need a smaller font rather than deletion.

Word document problems

Lesson 75 Dots and paragraph symbols appear in Word

What the problem means

Formatting marks are visible; they are editing aids rather than typed content.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click the Home tab. What you should see: Home controls appear.

2. Find the paragraph symbol in the Paragraph group. What you should see: You identify Show or Hide.

3. Click that symbol once. What you should see: Formatting marks toggle off.

4. Open File, then Print to check the preview. What you should see: You can verify the marks are not printed.

Check whether the fix worked

The editing symbols disappear from the normal view.

If it still does not work

If some marks remain, open Word Options, Display and inspect which marks are always shown.

Word document problems

Lesson 76 Pasted text has the wrong font and spacing

What the problem means

Paste may bring formatting from the source into your document.

Fix it one step at a time

1. If you just pasted, press Ctrl and Z once to undo that paste. What you should see: The pasted block is removed.

2. Place the cursor where the text belongs. What you should see: The insertion point is correct.

3. Click Home, then the arrow under Paste. What you should see: Paste choices appear.

4. Choose Keep Text Only when available. What you should see: Text is inserted without the source’s styling.

5. Read the result and reapply intended headings or emphasis. What you should see: You restore meaningful structure.

Check whether the fix worked

The pasted text matches the surrounding document.

If it still does not work

Keep Text Only removes tables and special formatting. Use a copy when testing on a complex document.

Word document problems

Lesson 77 Word text is too tiny to read

What the problem means

Document zoom can change the view without changing the actual font.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open the document in Word. What you should see: Its page appears.

2. Find the zoom slider at the bottom right. What you should see: You can see the current zoom percentage.

3. Click its plus button a few times or move the slider right. What you should see: The view becomes larger.

4. Stop when you can read comfortably. What you should see: The document remains at its actual font size.

Check whether the fix worked

The view is readable without changing the document’s fonts.

If it still does not work

If the printout is tiny too, inspect the actual font size or print scaling instead.

Word document problems

Lesson 78 A paragraph has too much space after it

What the problem means

Paragraph spacing can create gaps even without blank lines.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click within the affected paragraph. What you should see: Word places the cursor there.

2. Click the Layout tab. What you should see: Paragraph spacing controls appear.

3. Find Spacing Before and After. What you should see: You can read the current values.

4. Record those values, then reduce an excessive After value to an appropriate smaller value. What you should see: The gap decreases.

5. Check the adjacent paragraphs before saving. What you should see: You can judge the consistency.

Check whether the fix worked

The unwanted gap is reduced while paragraph text remains intact.

If it still does not work

If spacing is controlled by a style, revise that style consistently rather than adjusting every paragraph separately.

Word document problems

Lesson 79 Word underlines words in the wrong language

What the problem means

The proofing language may not match the text.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Select the affected paragraph by dragging across it. What you should see: That text is highlighted.

2. Click Review on the ribbon. What you should see: Proofing controls appear.

3. Click Language, then Set Proofing Language. What you should see: A language list opens.

4. Choose the language used in that paragraph and click OK. What you should see: Word applies that proofing language.

5. Check the underlined words again. What you should see: The proofing results update.

Check whether the fix worked

Correctly spelled words in the selected language are no longer flagged incorrectly.

If it still does not work

Proper names can still be flagged. Do not turn off all spell checking just to remove a few name warnings.

Word document problems

Lesson 80 Word says Unlicensed Product

What the problem means

Desktop Office may be signed into the wrong account or lack an active license.

Fix it one step at a time

1. In Word, click File. What you should see: The file menu appears.

2. Click Account. What you should see: The signed-in account and product information appear.

3. Read the account email and activation message. What you should see: You can identify a mismatch or expired entitlement.

4. If you own a license under another account, use the sign-in or switch-account option to enter that account. What you should see: Office checks that account’s license.

5. Close and reopen Word when requested. What you should see: You can check whether activation updates.

Check whether the fix worked

Office recognizes your valid license, or you have identified that no active entitlement is present.

If it still does not work

Do not enter a borrowed activation key. If you do not have a license, use an available permitted web editor or another editor for your own files.

Excel worksheet problems

Lesson 81 Excel displays hash marks instead of a number

What the problem means

A column may be too narrow; negative date or time results can also show hash marks.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click the cell displaying hash marks. What you should see: Its full value or formula appears in the formula bar.

2. Locate the column letter above that cell. What you should see: You identify the affected column.

3. Move the pointer to the right boundary of that column heading. What you should see: The pointer becomes a width-adjustment arrow.

4. Double-click that boundary. What you should see: Excel fits the column to its content.

5. Read the cell again. What you should see: You can check whether the value is now visible.

Check whether the fix worked

The value is displayed after widening, or you identify a negative date or time result.

If it still does not work

If widening does not help, inspect the underlying value and number format rather than replacing it blindly.

Excel worksheet problems

Lesson 82 Excel shows formulas instead of results

What the problem means

Show Formulas may be on for the worksheet.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open the affected worksheet. What you should see: Its cells appear.

2. Click the Formulas tab. What you should see: Formula tools appear.

3. Find Show Formulas in the Formula Auditing group. What you should see: You can see its toggle button.

4. If active, click it once. What you should see: Cells display calculated results again.

5. Check two or three formula cells. What you should see: You verify the view changed across the sheet.

Check whether the fix worked

Formula cells show results instead of formula text.

If it still does not work

If only one formula remains as text, check whether that cell is formatted as Text and whether its entry starts with an equals sign.

Excel worksheet problems

Lesson 83 Excel totals do not change after editing

What the problem means

The workbook may be set to manual calculation.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click Formulas on the Excel ribbon. What you should see: Formula controls appear.

2. Click Calculation Options. What you should see: Calculation choices open.

3. Select Automatic. What you should see: Excel recalculates when dependent inputs change.

4. Change one known input in a practice copy. What you should see: You have a controlled test.

5. Check the dependent total and undo the test input if needed. What you should see: You can verify recalculation without altering real records.

Check whether the fix worked

The total updates after a relevant input changes.

If it still does not work

If not, inspect whether the formula references that input. For a large workbook, ask its owner before changing intended manual calculation.

Excel worksheet problems

Lesson 84 Excel ignores numbers in a sum

What the problem means

Some entries may be stored as text rather than numeric values.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click an affected number cell. What you should see: Its value appears in the formula bar.

2. If a green triangle and warning button appear, click the warning button. What you should see: Excel explains the warning.

3. Choose Convert to Number if the warning says Number stored as text. What you should see: The value becomes numeric.

4. Repeat for the relevant selected cells if appropriate. What you should see: Those entries can participate in calculations.

5. Check the SUM total again. What you should see: You can compare the result.

Check whether the fix worked

The intended numeric entries are included in the total.

If it still does not work

Do not convert account numbers, ZIP codes, or identifiers just because they contain digits. If no warning appears, inspect a copy before bulk conversion.

Excel worksheet problems

Lesson 85 Excel shows DIV zero in a formula

What the problem means

The formula is dividing by a zero or empty denominator.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click the cell showing #DIV/0!. What you should see: The formula appears in the formula bar.

2. Read the reference after the division slash. What you should see: You identify the denominator cell or expression.

3. Click that referenced cell and inspect its value. What you should see: You can see whether it is blank or zero.

4. If a valid value is missing, enter the correct source value. What you should see: The denominator is corrected.

5. Return to the formula cell and check the result. What you should see: The formula recalculates.

Check whether the fix worked

The error clears when a legitimate nonzero denominator is present.

If it still does not work

If zero is a valid case, design an explicit zero-case formula in a copy. Do not invent a value just to hide the error.

Excel worksheet problems

Lesson 86 Excel shows a REF error

What the problem means

A formula may refer to cells removed by deleting a row or column.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click the cell showing #REF!. What you should see: The formula bar displays the broken reference.

2. If you just deleted a row or column, press Ctrl and Z once. What you should see: The recent deletion is undone.

3. Check whether the formula result returns. What you should see: You can confirm that deletion caused it.

4. If undo is no longer appropriate, compare the formula with a saved version or neighboring valid formula. What you should see: You identify the intended reference.

5. Correct the reference only when you know which data belongs there. What you should see: The formula points to valid cells.

Check whether the fix worked

The formula refers to the intended data and calculates again.

If it still does not work

Do not copy a nearby formula blindly; its row or column references may differ.

Excel worksheet problems

Lesson 87 Excel shows a NAME error

What the problem means

A function name, named range, or text syntax may be incorrect.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click the cell showing #NAME?. What you should see: Its formula appears in the formula bar.

2. Read the function name immediately after the equals sign. What you should see: You can spot a misspelled function.

3. Compare that name with Excel’s function suggestions while editing a copy. What you should see: Excel shows recognized function names.

4. Correct the spelling or the known missing quotation marks for text. What you should see: The formula syntax changes.

5. Press Enter and check the result. What you should see: Excel evaluates the corrected entry.

Check whether the fix worked

The formula uses recognized names and the error disappears.

If it still does not work

If the formula uses a custom named range, confirm that range exists. An unsupported newer function may require a compatible Excel version.

Excel worksheet problems

Lesson 88 Excel prints a sheet across too many pages

What the problem means

Print scaling or the selected print area may be too broad.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Press Ctrl and P in Excel. What you should see: Print preview opens.

2. Read the page count and look at the preview. What you should see: You can see how the sheet is split.

3. Open the scaling dropdown under Settings. What you should see: Scaling choices appear.

4. Choose Fit All Columns on One Page for a sheet that is too wide. What you should see: The preview fits the width while allowing multiple pages in height.

5. Check whether the text is still readable before printing. What you should see: You can judge whether scaling is practical.

Check whether the fix worked

The preview has the intended width and readable text.

If it still does not work

If text becomes tiny, use landscape orientation or print only the relevant selected range. Avoid forcing a huge sheet onto one page.

Excel worksheet problems

Lesson 89 Excel rows or columns seem missing

What the problem means

Rows or columns may be hidden, or a filter may exclude records.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Look at the row numbers and column letters for gaps. What you should see: You can identify hidden positions.

2. Select the headings on both sides of a gap by dragging across them. What you should see: The neighboring rows or columns are selected.

3. Right-click the selected headings. What you should see: Their context menu opens.

4. Click Unhide if shown. What you should see: Hidden rows or columns become visible.

5. If row numbers are still skipped and a filter is active, use Data, then Clear to clear the filter in a copy. What you should see: Filtered-out rows return.

Check whether the fix worked

The expected rows or columns are visible.

If it still does not work

Clearing a filter changes the view. Confirm with the workbook owner before changing a shared working view.

Excel worksheet problems

Lesson 90 Scrolling in Excel moves the sheet instead of the cell

What the problem means

Scroll Lock can change how the arrow keys behave.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click a worksheet cell. What you should see: The cell is selected.

2. Press an arrow key and observe whether selection moves or the sheet scrolls. What you should see: You can confirm the symptom.

3. If your keyboard has Scroll Lock, press it once. What you should see: Scroll Lock toggles.

4. If there is no key, click Start, type On-Screen Keyboard, and open it. What you should see: A virtual keyboard appears.

5. Click ScrLk on the virtual keyboard if active. What you should see: Scroll Lock switches off.

6. Return to Excel and press an arrow key. What you should see: The selection should move to the next cell.

Check whether the fix worked

Arrow keys move the selected cell normally.

If it still does not work

If not, check whether you are editing a formula or whether the keyboard itself is malfunctioning.

Gmail and email problems

Lesson 91 An expected email is missing

What the problem means

The message may be in Spam, Trash, another category, or a different account.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open Chrome and type mail.google.com in the top address bar, then press Enter. What you should see: The official Gmail page opens.

2. Sign in to your own account if asked. What you should see: Your mailbox appears.

3. Click your profile picture in the upper right and read the account email. What you should see: You can confirm the correct inbox.

4. Click the search box near the top. What you should see: A search cursor appears.

5. Type in:anywhere followed by a space and the sender’s email address, then press Enter. What you should see: Gmail searches across folders including Spam and Trash.

6. Open a matching message and check its date. What you should see: You can confirm whether it is the expected message.

Check whether the fix worked

You locate the email or confirm it is absent from this account.

If it still does not work

If it never arrived, ask the sender to verify your exact address and check for a bounce message.

Gmail and email problems

Lesson 92 Gmail says storage is full

What the problem means

Google account storage is shared across Gmail, Drive, and Photos.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open Chrome and type mail.google.com in the top address bar, then press Enter. What you should see: The official Gmail page opens.

2. Sign in to your own account if asked. What you should see: Your mailbox appears.

3. Read the storage warning shown in Gmail. What you should see: You confirm the problem is account storage.

4. Click the storage or Manage storage link in that warning. What you should see: The account storage overview opens.

5. Read which service uses the most space. What you should see: You can decide what to review.

6. Download a backup of any important file before deleting it. What you should see: You preserve needed information.

7. Remove only items you have reviewed and no longer need. What you should see: You free space without deleting unknown records.

8. Review Trash before emptying it if permanent deletion is needed for space. What you should see: You understand what would be permanently removed.

Check whether the fix worked

Account storage falls below its limit and mail can resume after the storage update takes effect.

If it still does not work

Storage changes may take time to update. Do not erase your entire mailbox to remove one warning.

Gmail and email problems

Lesson 93 An email comes back undelivered

What the problem means

A bounce message explains why a server rejected or could not deliver mail.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open Chrome and type mail.google.com in the top address bar, then press Enter. What you should see: The official Gmail page opens.

2. Sign in to your own account if asked. What you should see: Your mailbox appears.

3. Open the delivery failure message in the inbox. What you should see: Its error details appear.

4. Find the rejected recipient address and reason. What you should see: You identify the destination and failure.

5. Compare the address with the intended recipient’s confirmed address. What you should see: You can spot a typo.

6. If mistyped, create a corrected message to that confirmed address. What you should see: You can retry the valid destination.

7. If the reason is mailbox full or server unavailable, wait or contact the recipient another way. What you should see: You avoid repeated identical failures.

Check whether the fix worked

The corrected message is delivered, or you identify a recipient-side failure.

If it still does not work

For a blocked message or attachment, read the stated policy. Do not evade a security block by disguising a file.

Gmail and email problems

Lesson 94 An attachment never finishes uploading

What the problem means

The internet connection or file upload may be interrupted.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open Chrome and type mail.google.com in the top address bar, then press Enter. What you should see: The official Gmail page opens.

2. Sign in to your own account if asked. What you should see: Your mailbox appears.

3. Open the saved draft. What you should see: The composition window appears.

4. Look for upload progress or an error beside the attachment. What you should see: You can tell whether it finished.

5. Do not click Send while the attachment is still uploading. What you should see: You avoid sending before completion.

6. Try a familiar website in another tab. What you should see: You test the internet connection.

7. If the upload has failed, remove that failed attachment with its X and attach the trusted file again. What you should see: A new upload begins.

8. Wait until its name appears without progress, then review the message. What you should see: You can confirm upload completion.

Check whether the fix worked

The file is attached and finished uploading before you send.

If it still does not work

If repeatedly failing, check its size and permitted type. Save the draft before restarting the browser.

Gmail and email problems

Lesson 95 You cannot find the attachment in an email

What the problem means

The attachment may be farther down the message or absent from the sender’s email.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open Chrome and type mail.google.com in the top address bar, then press Enter. What you should see: The official Gmail page opens.

2. Sign in to your own account if asked. What you should see: Your mailbox appears.

3. Open the message that should contain the attachment. What you should see: The email body appears.

4. Scroll to the bottom of that individual message. What you should see: Attachment cards usually appear below its text.

5. If the email is a conversation, expand the particular message from the sender. What you should see: Its own attachments become visible.

6. Click the attachment’s download arrow if present. What you should see: The file downloads.

7. Press Ctrl and J to locate the download. What you should see: You can find the saved file.

Check whether the fix worked

You locate and download the intended attachment.

If it still does not work

If no attachment exists, ask the sender to resend it. Do not click an unfamiliar download link merely because it claims to be an attachment.

Gmail and email problems

Lesson 96 Gmail opened the wrong account

What the problem means

Several signed-in Google accounts can make the browser choose another inbox.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open Chrome and type mail.google.com in the top address bar, then press Enter. What you should see: The official Gmail page opens.

2. Sign in to your own account if asked. What you should see: Your mailbox appears.

3. Click the profile picture in the upper right. What you should see: The signed-in account list appears.

4. Read the email address of the current account. What you should see: You identify which mailbox is open.

5. Click the intended account in the list if present. What you should see: Gmail switches to that account.

6. If absent, choose Add another account and sign into your own account. What you should see: The intended mailbox becomes available.

7. Check the profile email again. What you should see: You verify the account switch.

Check whether the fix worked

You are viewing the intended inbox.

If it still does not work

Keep personal and business addresses clearly labeled. Confirm the From address before sending a business message.

Gmail and email problems

Lesson 97 An email was deleted accidentally

What the problem means

Gmail Trash may still contain a deleted message.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open Chrome and type mail.google.com in the top address bar, then press Enter. What you should see: The official Gmail page opens.

2. Sign in to your own account if asked. What you should see: Your mailbox appears.

3. In the left folder list, click More if Trash is hidden. What you should see: Additional folders appear.

4. Click Trash. What you should see: Deleted messages are listed.

5. Find and open the intended message. What you should see: You can inspect its content.

6. Click Move to and choose Inbox. What you should see: The message returns to the inbox.

7. Open Inbox and locate it. What you should see: You verify restoration.

Check whether the fix worked

The message appears in Inbox again.

If it still does not work

Messages already permanently deleted may not be recoverable. Act promptly and check the correct account.

Gmail and email problems

Lesson 98 Gmail appears frozen or shows a temporary error

What the problem means

The browser session or Gmail service may have a temporary problem.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open Chrome and type mail.google.com in the top address bar, then press Enter. What you should see: The official Gmail page opens.

2. Sign in to your own account if asked. What you should see: Your mailbox appears.

3. Read and record the error message. What you should see: You know the exact symptom.

4. Wait briefly, then press Ctrl and R once. What you should see: Gmail reloads.

5. If unchanged, open a familiar unrelated site in another tab. What you should see: You check whether the connection works.

6. Press Ctrl, Shift, and N together and open mail.google.com there. What you should see: You can test Gmail in an Incognito session.

7. Sign in to your account in that window if needed. What you should see: You compare a separate session.

Check whether the fix worked

Gmail loads normally in one session or you identify a broader connection failure.

If it still does not work

If Gmail alone remains unavailable, check its official service status or wait before retrying. Avoid repeatedly deleting browser data.

Gmail and email problems

Lesson 99 A legitimate sender keeps going to Spam

What the problem means

Gmail may have misclassified a message.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open Chrome and type mail.google.com in the top address bar, then press Enter. What you should see: The official Gmail page opens.

2. Sign in to your own account if asked. What you should see: Your mailbox appears.

3. Click More in the left list if needed, then click Spam. What you should see: Filtered messages appear.

4. Open the message and verify the sender’s actual email address. What you should see: You can check that it is the expected sender.

5. If legitimate, click Report not spam. What you should see: Gmail moves it out of Spam.

6. Check Inbox for that message. What you should see: You verify its new location.

Check whether the fix worked

The legitimate message is restored to the inbox.

If it still does not work

Do not mark a suspicious message safe because it displays a familiar name. The actual address and expected content matter.

Gmail and email problems

Lesson 100 You sent the wrong email and want to stop it

What the problem means

Gmail’s Undo Send control appears only briefly after sending.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Immediately after sending, look at the message confirmation near the lower left of Gmail. What you should see: It may show Message sent with an Undo option.

2. If Undo is still visible, click it immediately. What you should see: Gmail cancels the pending send and reopens the draft.

3. Correct the recipient, attachment, or wording in the draft. What you should see: You can repair the mistake.

4. Read the whole draft again before sending. What you should see: You verify the correction.

Check whether the fix worked

Undo reopens the draft while available; otherwise the message has already left.

If it still does not work

Once Undo disappears, it cannot reliably recall the message. Send a clear correction if needed rather than assuming it was withdrawn.

Official help for further troubleshooting

Checked September 29 2026. Use these official references when you need a deeper diagnostic or your menu differs. The lesson explanations and wording are written for this classroom; these support pages provide the underlying product guidance.

Google Chrome connection and loading errors https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/6098869

Chrome crashes and startup problems https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/142063

Chrome settings https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/17561599

Windows Wi Fi connection problems https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/connectivity-networking/fix-wi-fi-connection-issues-in-windows

Windows audio problems https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/hardware/audio/fix-sound-or-audio-problems-in-windows

Windows mouse and keyboard problems https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/hardware/input-devices/mouse-and-keyboard-problems-in-windows

Windows Bluetooth problems https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/hardware/bluetooth/fix-bluetooth-problems-in-windows

Office read only files https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/collab-files/why-did-my-file-open-read-only

Word blank pages https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/word/delete-a-blank-page

Excel formula problems https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/how-to-avoid-broken-formulas-in-excel

Gmail missing messages https://support.google.com/mail/answer/7015314

Gmail attachments https://support.google.com/mail/answer/6584

Gmail delivery failures https://support.google.com/mail/answer/6596

title: Technical Troubleshooting Classroom 100 Lessons — Step-by-step
content:
Technical Troubleshooting Classroom

100 common computer problems with step by step fixes

Detailed step format used in this revision

• Every action is kept in the original order.

• Complete one numbered action at a time. Do not jump ahead.

• For each action, the added click-by-click breakdown tells you what to click, what to type, and what to check.

• After changing a file, press Ctrl+S unless the lesson specifically tells you not to save yet.

• If your screen does not match the written checkpoint, stop on that step and correct it before continuing.

Prepared for Templar Hughes Bryant

How to use your classroom

Find the lesson matching the problem you actually see. Each lesson names the symptom, explains likely causes, gives numbered actions, describes what should appear, and shows how to test the result. These are first troubleshooting steps; some failures need a technician or the service provider.

Work through one step at a time. After the action, read “What you should see.” If your screen differs, stop there and write down the message or show that screen when asking for help. Do not continue just because the next step is printed.

The steps primarily use Windows 11, desktop Microsoft Word and Excel, Chrome, and Gmail in a browser. Word and Excel lessons apply only when those apps are available. Labels can differ by version. For Windows 10, Devices replaces Bluetooth & devices in many paths; Privacy replaces Privacy & security, and Update & Security contains Windows Update.

Before restarting or ending an app, save any work you can. Before testing a document change, save a copy. A plus sign in a keyboard shortcut means hold the first key while pressing the others. The Windows key has the Windows logo.

The original 50 lessons have been rewritten with more detail. Lessons 51 through 100 add new browser, display, Word, Excel, and email problems. This workbook contains 100 lessons in total; your separate original Chrome lesson remains a worked example.

Lesson guide 1 to 25

1. Search engine changes back by itself

2. Chrome opens unwanted pages at startup

3. A website will not load

4. A page keeps showing an old version

5. Chrome says Aw Snap

6. Chrome is unusually slow

7. A Chrome extension changes pages

8. Chrome will not download a file

9. A website cannot use the microphone

10. Text on a website looks too large

11. Wi-Fi is disconnected

12. Wi-Fi says connected but websites fail

13. Only one website is unreachable

14. Airplane mode blocks connections

15. The wrong Wi-Fi network is selected

16. Wi-Fi password is rejected

17. Internet drops repeatedly

18. A VPN makes a site fail

19. A wired connection is not working

20. Wi-Fi is unavailable or will not reconnect

21. A downloaded file seems missing

22. You cannot find a saved document

23. A file opens in the wrong app

24. A folder looks empty

25. The computer says storage is low

Lesson guide 26 to 50

26. A file will not delete

27. A file was deleted by mistake

28. A USB drive does not appear

29. File extensions are hidden

30. A file is too large to email

31. Speakers make no sound

32. Sound plays through the wrong device

33. Microphone records nothing

34. Camera shows a black picture

35. Bluetooth headphones will not connect

36. A printer is offline

37. A print job is stuck

38. The wrong printer is selected

39. Mouse pointer feels too fast

40. Keyboard types unexpected characters

41. An app is frozen

42. The computer is slow after startup

43. Windows Update is stuck

44. A program will not open

45. You forgot a website password

46. A password reset email does not arrive

47. An account says the password is wrong

48. A suspicious pop-up says the PC is infected

49. A Windows notification keeps appearing

50. Windows shows the wrong date or time

Lesson guide 51 to 75

51. Chrome says it needs an update

52. You closed a browser tab by mistake

53. A website keeps asking you to sign in

54. A website sends unwanted notifications

55. A legitimate pop-up window is blocked

56. A video on a webpage has no sound

57. A PDF opens in Chrome when you wanted to save it

58. A webpage form lost your typed information

59. Chrome saved the wrong password

60. A page says your connection is not private

61. Everything on the screen is too small

62. The screen is too dim

63. The picture looks stretched or blurry

64. A second monitor shows no picture

65. The desktop appears on the wrong monitor

66. The screen is sideways

67. The mouse stops responding

68. The laptop touchpad does not move the pointer

69. The number keypad will not type numbers

70. A USB accessory works poorly through a hub

71. Word will not let you edit a downloaded document

72. Word opens a document as read only

73. Word changes disappeared after a crash

74. Word has an unwanted blank page

75. Dots and paragraph symbols appear in Word

Lesson guide 76 to 100

76. Pasted text has the wrong font and spacing

77. Word text is too tiny to read

78. A paragraph has too much space after it

79. Word underlines words in the wrong language

80. Word says Unlicensed Product

81. Excel displays hash marks instead of a number

82. Excel shows formulas instead of results

83. Excel totals do not change after editing

84. Excel ignores numbers in a sum

85. Excel shows DIV zero in a formula

86. Excel shows a REF error

87. Excel shows a NAME error

88. Excel prints a sheet across too many pages

89. Excel rows or columns seem missing

90. Scrolling in Excel moves the sheet instead of the cell

91. An expected email is missing

92. Gmail says storage is full

93. An email comes back undelivered

94. An attachment never finishes uploading

95. You cannot find the attachment in an email

96. Gmail opened the wrong account

97. An email was deleted accidentally

98. Gmail appears frozen or shows a temporary error

99. A legitimate sender keeps going to Spam

100. You sent the wrong email and want to stop it

Chrome and websites

Lesson 1 Search engine changes back by itself

What the problem means

An extension or installed program may be changing Chrome settings again.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open Google Chrome. What you should see: A browser window appears.

2. Click the three dots in the upper right corner. What you should see: The Chrome menu opens.

3. Click Settings. What you should see: A Settings tab opens.

4. Click Search engine in the Settings menu. What you should see: The Search engine page appears.

5. Read the current search engine name. Write it down before changing it. What you should see: You have a record of the original choice.

6. Click Change beside the current choice. What you should see: A list of search engines opens.

7. Select the engine you prefer and confirm if asked. What you should see: The selected name appears on the Settings page.

8. Close Chrome, reopen it, and try a new search from the long address bar at the top. What you should see: The search uses your chosen engine.

9. If it changes back, click the three dots, then Extensions, then Manage extensions. What you should see: A list of installed extensions appears.

10. Switch off one search-related extension you recognize. Set the engine again and retry. What you should see: You can compare behavior with that extension off.

Check whether the fix worked

The setting stays saved after reopening Chrome; record the extension involved if it changes only when switched on.

If it still does not work

If the choice is locked or the extension is managed, record the message and ask the computer administrator. Do not keep changing unrelated settings.

Chrome and websites

Lesson 2 Chrome opens unwanted pages at startup

What the problem means

A startup page setting may tell Chrome to reopen an old site.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open Google Chrome. What you should see: A browser window appears.

2. Click the three dots in the upper right corner. What you should see: The Chrome menu opens.

3. Click Settings. What you should see: A Settings tab opens.

4. Click On startup in the Settings menu. What you should see: The On startup page appears.

5. Read the selected startup option. What you should see: You can see whether Chrome restores tabs or opens specific pages.

6. Select Open the New Tab page. What you should see: The selection dot moves beside that option.

7. Click the three dots, then Exit. Reopen Chrome. What you should see: A new tab should open instead of the unwanted page.

Check whether the fix worked

Chrome starts on the page you chose.

If it still does not work

If the unwanted page returns, inspect extensions as in Lesson 1.

Chrome and websites

Lesson 3 A website will not load

What the problem means

The problem may belong to one page, Chrome, or the connection.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click the long address bar at the top of Chrome. Check the spelling of the website address. What you should see: You can see the actual address you are visiting.

2. Hold Ctrl and press R to reload. What you should see: The page tries to load again.

3. Click the plus sign beside the tabs to open a new tab. What you should see: A blank tab opens.

4. Type the address of a different familiar website and press Enter. What you should see: You find out whether another site can load.

5. Hold Ctrl and Shift, then press N. What you should see: A dark Incognito window opens.

6. Type the original site address there and press Enter. What you should see: You can compare the same site in a separate browser session.

Check whether the fix worked

Record which sites work and whether Incognito changes the result.

If it still does not work

If all sites fail, go to the internet lessons. If only one fails, record its error and try again later.

Chrome and websites

Lesson 4 A page keeps showing an old version

What the problem means

Chrome may be showing stored page data.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open the page showing old content. What you should see: You can see the outdated information.

2. Hold Ctrl and press R. What you should see: Chrome reloads the page.

3. If unchanged, hold Ctrl and Shift and press R. What you should see: Chrome requests a fresh page copy.

4. Close that tab with its X, then open the site again in a new tab. What you should see: The page is loaded in a new tab.

Check whether the fix worked

The page shows its current content; if not, the site itself may not have updated.

If it still does not work

If it still shows the old version, the website or its server cache may not have updated. Do not erase all browser data first.

Chrome and websites

Lesson 5 Chrome says Aw Snap

What the problem means

A tab crashed, often because of a temporary page or memory problem.

Fix it one step at a time

1. On the Aw Snap page, click Reload. What you should see: Chrome attempts to reopen the page.

2. Close unused tabs by clicking their tab X buttons. What you should see: Fewer pages remain open.

3. Save work in other apps before closing them. What you should see: Your documents are preserved.

4. Click Chrome’s three dots, then Exit. What you should see: The browser closes.

5. Open Chrome and visit the same page. What you should see: You can check whether the crash repeats.

Check whether the fix worked

The page stays open without crashing.

If it still does not work

If it crashes repeatedly on only one site, record the address and error. If many sites crash, check Chrome updates in Lesson 51.

Chrome and websites

Lesson 6 Chrome is unusually slow

What the problem means

Too many tabs, extensions, or background apps can consume memory.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click the X on browser tabs you are finished using. What you should see: The tab count decreases.

2. Save work in other open programs. What you should see: You can close those apps without losing work.

3. Close unused apps with the X in each app window. What you should see: Fewer apps are running.

4. Return to Chrome and reload the slow page with Ctrl and R. What you should see: You can compare its response time.

5. Try a different simple website. What you should see: You can tell whether the slowdown belongs to one page.

Check whether the fix worked

Pages respond faster; note if one particular page remains slow.

If it still does not work

If the entire computer is slow, see the Windows startup lesson. Record when the slowdown begins.

Chrome and websites

Lesson 7 A Chrome extension changes pages

What the problem means

An extension can affect searches or page loading.

Fix it one step at a time

1. In Chrome, click the three dots in the upper right. What you should see: The browser menu opens.

2. Click Extensions, then Manage extensions. What you should see: Installed extensions appear as cards.

3. Read each name and locate the extension you suspect. What you should see: You know which switch you will change.

4. Click that extension’s on and off switch once to turn it off. What you should see: Its switch appears off.

5. Reload the affected page with Ctrl and R. What you should see: You can test the change.

6. If it made no difference, turn that extension back on. What you should see: The original extension setting is restored.

Check whether the fix worked

The behavior changes only while a specific extension is off.

If it still does not work

Test one extension at a time. If a specific extension causes the problem, check its publisher and settings before deciding whether to remove it.

Chrome and websites

Lesson 8 Chrome will not download a file

What the problem means

The site, destination, or a safety warning may be involved.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Press Ctrl+J. For a shortcut with a plus sign, hold the first key while pressing the next, then release them. What you should see: Chrome’s Downloads page opens.

2. Read the message beside the failed file. What you should see: You know whether the issue is a network error, blocked file, or interrupted download.

3. Open another familiar website in a new tab. What you should see: You can confirm the internet connection works.

4. If the file is from a trusted source and only the download was interrupted, click Retry if shown. What you should see: Chrome attempts the download again.

5. When finished, click Show in folder. What you should see: File Explorer displays the downloaded file.

Check whether the fix worked

The file appears in Downloads; never bypass a warning for an unknown file.

If it still does not work

Do not bypass a security warning for an unknown file. Record the exact download error if Retry fails.

Chrome and websites

Lesson 9 A website cannot use the microphone

What the problem means

The site or Windows may lack microphone permission.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open the trusted website that needs your microphone. What you should see: Its address is visible at the top of Chrome.

2. Click the controls icon immediately to the left of the website address. What you should see: A small site information panel opens.

3. Click Site settings. What you should see: Permissions for that site open.

4. Find Microphone and select Allow if you want this site to use it. What you should see: The permission shows Allow.

5. Return to the website tab and reload it. What you should see: The updated permission takes effect.

6. Click the site’s microphone test or recording button and speak. What you should see: The site should show an audio level or recording.

Check whether the fix worked

The site detects your voice; if not, see the microphone lesson.

If it still does not work

If it still receives no sound, use Lesson 33 to check the Windows input device.

Chrome and websites

Lesson 10 Text on a website looks too large

What the problem means

The browser zoom may have changed accidentally.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click anywhere on the affected webpage away from a text box. What you should see: The page is active.

2. Hold Ctrl and press the zero key on the number row. What you should see: Chrome restores page zoom to 100 percent.

3. If you need larger text, hold Ctrl and press the plus key once. What you should see: The page becomes larger.

4. Repeat once at a time until comfortable, or use Ctrl and minus to reduce it. What you should see: You can adjust without losing the page edges.

Check whether the fix worked

Text becomes comfortable to read without cutting off page controls.

If it still does not work

If everything in Windows is oversized, use the display scale lesson instead.

Internet and Wi-Fi

Lesson 11 Wi-Fi is disconnected

What the problem means

The computer may not be connected to your router.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click the network, speaker, or battery area near the clock in the lower right. What you should see: Quick settings opens.

2. If Wi-Fi is off, click its button to turn it on. What you should see: Wi-Fi becomes available.

3. Click the arrow beside the Wi-Fi button. What you should see: Nearby networks are listed.

4. Click your own network name. What you should see: Connection options appear.

5. Click Connect. If asked, enter your Wi-Fi password and click Next. What you should see: Windows attempts to join the network.

6. Open a familiar website. What you should see: You can test actual internet access.

Check whether the fix worked

The network says Connected and a familiar website opens.

If it still does not work

If the network says Connected but websites fail, continue with Lesson 12.

Internet and Wi-Fi

Lesson 12 Wi-Fi says connected but websites fail

What the problem means

The router may be reachable while internet access is unavailable.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open two familiar websites in separate browser tabs. What you should see: You can check whether more than one website fails.

2. On your phone, connect to the same Wi-Fi and try a website. What you should see: You can compare another device on the same network.

3. On the PC, click the network area near the clock. What you should see: Quick settings opens.

4. Turn Wi-Fi off, wait about five seconds, then turn it on. What you should see: The wireless connection restarts.

5. Reconnect to your own network and try the website again. What you should see: You can test whether reconnecting helped.

Check whether the fix worked

If all devices fail, focus on the router or provider; if only the PC fails, continue PC diagnosis.

If it still does not work

If every device fails, check your router or internet provider. If only the PC fails, use the Windows network diagnostic steps in Lesson 20.

Internet and Wi-Fi

Lesson 13 Only one website is unreachable

What the problem means

The site may be down or its address may be wrong.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open a new Chrome tab with the plus sign beside the tabs. What you should see: A blank tab appears.

2. Type a different familiar website address and press Enter. What you should see: You can check whether the internet works generally.

3. Return to the failing site and check the address for spelling mistakes. What you should see: You can correct a wrong address.

4. Press Ctrl and R to reload. What you should see: The site tries again.

5. Press Ctrl, Shift, and N together, then try the site in that Incognito window. What you should see: You can compare a different browser session.

Check whether the fix worked

Other websites work; record the exact error on the failing one.

If it still does not work

If the site alone fails, record the error and retry later. A single site failure does not prove your router is broken.

Internet and Wi-Fi

Lesson 14 Airplane mode blocks connections

What the problem means

Airplane mode disables wireless connections.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click the network area beside the Windows clock. What you should see: Quick settings opens.

2. Find Airplane mode. What you should see: You can read whether it is on.

3. If it is on, click the Airplane mode button once. What you should see: Airplane mode switches off.

4. Click Wi-Fi to turn it on, then click its arrow. What you should see: The network list appears.

5. Choose your network and click Connect. What you should see: Windows reconnects.

Check whether the fix worked

The Wi-Fi list is visible and a website opens.

If it still does not work

If Airplane mode is already off, do not toggle other settings randomly. Check the Wi-Fi lesson.

Internet and Wi-Fi

Lesson 15 The wrong Wi-Fi network is selected

What the problem means

A saved nearby network may connect automatically.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click the network area near the Windows clock. What you should see: Quick settings opens.

2. Click the arrow next to Wi-Fi. What you should see: Network names appear.

3. Read the name marked Connected. What you should see: You identify the current network.

4. Click your own network name. What you should see: Its connection options appear.

5. Click Connect and enter its password if asked. What you should see: Windows switches to your network.

Check whether the fix worked

The connected name matches your router and the internet works.

If it still does not work

If it keeps choosing another network, disconnect that network and clear its Connect automatically choice.

Internet and Wi-Fi

Lesson 16 Wi-Fi password is rejected

What the problem means

The password may contain a mistyped character or may have changed.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open the Wi-Fi network list from the network area beside the clock. What you should see: Nearby network names appear.

2. Select your own network and click Connect. What you should see: A password box appears if authentication is needed.

3. Read the network name again before typing. What you should see: You confirm the password is for the correct router.

4. Type the password using the correct uppercase and lowercase letters. What you should see: Characters appear as dots or symbols.

5. Use the eye icon if provided to check what you typed, then hide it again. What you should see: You can spot a typing mistake.

6. Click Next. What you should see: Windows attempts the connection.

Check whether the fix worked

Windows connects without asking again.

If it still does not work

If rejected again, obtain the current password from the network owner. Avoid repeated guesses.

Internet and Wi-Fi

Lesson 17 Internet drops repeatedly

What the problem means

The distance to the router or a local connection issue may be involved.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Write down the time when the connection drops. What you should see: You have a pattern to compare.

2. Move the computer closer to your router if practical. What you should see: You reduce distance and obstructions.

3. Repeat the task that usually loses connection. What you should see: You can see whether proximity helps.

4. Check whether a phone on the same Wi-Fi disconnects at the same time. What you should see: You can compare a second device.

5. Save work, click Start, click Power, and click Restart. What you should see: Windows restarts.

6. Reconnect and retry the task. What you should see: You can compare stability after restarting.

Check whether the fix worked

Compare stability near the router and on other devices before changing settings.

If it still does not work

If all devices disconnect together, ask the provider or router owner to investigate. If only this PC drops, record its wireless adapter and error.

Internet and Wi-Fi

Lesson 18 A VPN makes a site fail

What the problem means

A VPN can change the route a website sees.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click the Windows Start button on the taskbar. What you should see: The Start menu opens.

2. Click Settings. If it is not visible, type Settings and click the Settings app in the results. What you should see: The Windows Settings window opens.

3. Click Network & internet. What you should see: The Network & internet settings appear.

4. Click VPN. What you should see: The VPN settings appear.

5. Read whether a VPN connection shows Connected. What you should see: You know whether this test applies.

6. If it is your own VPN, click its connection and click Disconnect. What you should see: The VPN status changes.

7. Reload the failing website. What you should see: You can compare access without the VPN.

8. Reconnect the VPN when finished if you normally need it. What you should see: Your usual connection is restored.

Check whether the fix worked

Record whether the site works only without the VPN.

If it still does not work

For an employer-required VPN, ask the administrator before disconnecting it. A site that works only without it may need VPN support.

Internet and Wi-Fi

Lesson 19 A wired connection is not working

What the problem means

A loose cable or inactive port can break Ethernet access.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Locate the Ethernet cable plugged into your computer. What you should see: You identify the wired connection.

2. Push the connector in gently until secure. What you should see: It seats in the port.

3. Check the cable’s other end at the router and seat it firmly. What you should see: Both ends are connected.

4. If available, move the router end to another LAN port, not the WAN or Internet port. What you should see: You test another local port.

5. Open a familiar website. What you should see: You test internet access.

Check whether the fix worked

The network shows connected; if not, test another cable if you have one.

If it still does not work

If available, try a known working Ethernet cable. Report whether another device can use the same port.

Internet and Wi-Fi

Lesson 20 Wi-Fi is unavailable or will not reconnect

What the problem means

Windows may have a wireless adapter or connection problem. Its network diagnostic can help identify the cause.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click Start, type Get Help, and click the matching app in the results. What you should see: Get Help opens.

2. Click the app’s search box and type network and internet troubleshooter. What you should see: The search text appears.

3. Press Enter. What you should see: The app offers diagnostic prompts or support options.

4. Read each prompt and select the option matching your symptom. What you should see: The tool checks the relevant connection.

5. Record the diagnosis and test a familiar website. What you should see: You can check its result.

Check whether the fix worked

Record the diagnosis and whether the connection works.

If it still does not work

If Get Help cannot load online, record the symptom and compare another device. Do not use a full network reset as your first action.

Files and storage

Lesson 21 A downloaded file seems missing

What the problem means

The browser may have saved it in Downloads or another folder.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Press Ctrl+J. For a shortcut with a plus sign, hold the first key while pressing the next, then release them. What you should see: Chrome Downloads opens.

2. Find the file by its name and download date. What you should see: Its download entry is visible.

3. Click Show in folder beside that file. What you should see: File Explorer opens its saved location.

4. Read the folder path above the file list. What you should see: You know where the file actually lives.

Check whether the fix worked

You can see the file in its actual folder.

If it still does not work

If it is not in Chrome Downloads, open File Explorer and search Downloads and Documents by part of the name.

Files and storage

Lesson 22 You cannot find a saved document

What the problem means

The file may have been saved under a different name or folder.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Hold the Windows key and press E, then release both keys. What you should see: File Explorer opens. You can browse folders here.

2. Click Documents in the left pane. What you should see: Your document folder opens.

3. Click the search box in the upper right. What you should see: A text cursor appears in the search box.

4. Type a distinctive part of the filename and press Enter. What you should see: Matching files are listed.

5. Check Date modified and the file location before opening a result. What you should see: You can distinguish different copies.

6. Double-click the intended result. What you should see: The document opens.

Check whether the fix worked

Open the expected document and note its folder.
