If not found, repeat the search in Downloads and Desktop. Check the app’s recent file list too.

Files and storage

Lesson 23 A file opens in the wrong app

What the problem means

The file association may point to a different program.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Hold the Windows key and press E, then release both keys. What you should see: File Explorer opens. You can browse folders here.

2. Find the file and right-click its name. What you should see: A context menu opens.

3. Click Open with. If hidden, click Show more options first. What you should see: Available apps appear.

4. Click Choose another app. What you should see: An app selection window opens.

5. Select the app you want and click Just once. What you should see: The file opens without changing every file of that type.

Check whether the fix worked

The file opens correctly before you change a permanent default.

If it still does not work

If it works, repeat and choose Always if that is your preferred default. Do not change the file extension to force it open.

Files and storage

Lesson 24 A folder looks empty

What the problem means

You may be in a different folder or filtering the view.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Hold the Windows key and press E, then release both keys. What you should see: File Explorer opens. You can browse folders here.

2. Read the folder name and path near the top. What you should see: You can confirm where you are.

3. Click the Back arrow once if you may be in the wrong subfolder. What you should see: The previous folder appears.

4. If the upper-right search box contains text, clear it. What you should see: The view is no longer limited to search results.

5. Look again for the expected filenames. What you should see: You see the normal contents.

Check whether the fix worked

The expected filename appears or you identify the correct folder.

If it still does not work

If files are still absent, search by filename and check Recycle Bin. Do not assume the files are deleted just because a folder is empty.

Files and storage

Lesson 25 The computer says storage is low

What the problem means

Temporary files and large personal files may fill the drive.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click the Windows Start button on the taskbar. What you should see: The Start menu opens.

2. Click Settings. If it is not visible, type Settings and click the Settings app in the results. What you should see: The Windows Settings window opens.

3. Click System. What you should see: The System settings appear.

4. Click Storage. What you should see: The Storage settings appear.

5. Read the available space and the storage categories. What you should see: You can see what is taking space.

6. Click Temporary files. What you should see: Windows scans and lists removable categories.

7. Read each checked category. Leave Downloads unchecked unless you already reviewed those files. What you should see: You avoid accidentally removing personal downloads.

8. Select only categories you understand, then click Remove files and confirm if asked. What you should see: Windows removes those selected items.

9. Return to Storage and read the free space again. What you should see: You can measure the result.

Check whether the fix worked

Free space increases and your personal files remain available.

If it still does not work

If still nearly full, review large personal files before moving them to a backup drive. Do not delete Windows or Program Files folders.

Files and storage

Lesson 26 A file will not delete

What the problem means

The file may be open in a program or require permission.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Close any program that is currently using the file. What you should see: The file should no longer be open in that app.

2. Hold the Windows key and press E, then release both keys. What you should see: File Explorer opens. You can browse folders here.

3. Find the file, click it once, and press Delete. What you should see: Windows tries to move it to Recycle Bin.

4. If a message names an app using it, record that app name and close it normally. What you should see: You know what is blocking deletion.

5. Try Delete again. What you should see: You can test after releasing the file.

Check whether the fix worked

The file moves to Recycle Bin; do not force-delete system files.

If it still does not work

If access is denied, stop and check ownership. Do not force-delete a system file or someone else’s file.

Files and storage

Lesson 27 A file was deleted by mistake

What the problem means

Recycle Bin often holds recently deleted local files.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click Start, type Recycle Bin, and click the matching app in the results. What you should see: Recycle Bin opens.

2. Find the file by name or Date deleted. What you should see: You locate the deleted item.

3. Right-click the correct file. What you should see: Its menu appears.

4. Click Restore. What you should see: Windows returns it to its original folder.

5. Open that original folder and double-click the file. What you should see: You verify it is readable.

Check whether the fix worked

The file is back in its original location.

If it still does not work

If not in Recycle Bin, check your backup or cloud recycle bin. Stop writing new files to a drive if valuable data may need recovery.

Files and storage

Lesson 28 A USB drive does not appear

What the problem means

The connection, port, or drive may be the problem.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Disconnect and reconnect the USB drive carefully. What you should see: Windows may play a connection sound.

2. Hold the Windows key and press E, then release both keys. What you should see: File Explorer opens. You can browse folders here.

3. Click This PC in the left pane. What you should see: Internal and connected drives appear.

4. Look under Devices and drives for the USB drive. What you should see: You can tell whether Windows sees it.

5. If absent, try another USB port on the computer. What you should see: You test a different port.

6. If possible, test the same drive on another computer. What you should see: You compare whether the drive itself responds.

Check whether the fix worked

The drive appears under This PC; do not format it if it contains needed files.

If it still does not work

If Windows asks to format a drive containing needed files, cancel. Formatting is not a safe first recovery step.

Files and storage

Lesson 29 File extensions are hidden

What the problem means

Hidden endings can make different file types look alike, or make a name seem incomplete.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Hold the Windows key and press E, then release both keys. What you should see: File Explorer opens. You can browse folders here.

2. Click View near the top of File Explorer. What you should see: View options open.

3. Point to or click Show. What you should see: More display choices appear.

4. Click File name extensions so a check mark appears. What you should see: Names now show endings such as .docx and .pdf.

5. Read the complete filename before opening it. What you should see: You can identify the actual file type.

Check whether the fix worked

You can distinguish the intended file from copies.

If it still does not work

On Windows 10, use the View tab and check File name extensions. Keep the extension when renaming a file.

Files and storage

Lesson 30 A file is too large to email

What the problem means

Attachment limits can reject large files.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Hold the Windows key and press E, then release both keys. What you should see: File Explorer opens. You can browse folders here.

2. Find the attachment file and right-click it. What you should see: Its menu appears.

3. Click Properties and read Size. What you should see: You know how large it is.

4. Close Properties. For several files, select them and right-click. What you should see: A file menu opens.

5. Click Compress to ZIP file if available; on Windows 10 use Send to, then Compressed zipped folder. What you should see: A ZIP copy appears.

6. Check the ZIP size before attaching it. What you should see: You can see whether compression reduced it.

Check whether the fix worked

The attachment is accepted or a share link opens for the intended recipient.

If it still does not work

If still too large, use an approved share link and give access only to the intended recipient. Photos and PDFs may compress very little.

Sound, camera, and devices

Lesson 31 Speakers make no sound

What the problem means

Windows may be muted or sending sound to another device.

Fix it one step at a time

2. Check whether the speaker symbol shows muted. What you should see: You can see the mute state.

5. Play a short familiar video. What you should see: You can test audible sound.

Sound comes from the speakers you selected.

Lesson 32 Sound plays through the wrong device

What the problem means

Windows may have selected headphones or a monitor.

Fix it one step at a time

3. Click System. What you should see: The System settings appear.

4. Click Sound. What you should see: The Sound settings appear.

5. Look under Output. What you should see: Available audio devices are listed.

Audio comes from the selected device.

Lesson 33 Microphone records nothing

What the problem means

The wrong input or privacy permission may be selected.

Fix it one step at a time

3. Click System. What you should see: The System settings appear.

4. Click Sound. What you should see: The Sound settings appear.

5. Scroll to Input. What you should see: Microphone choices appear.

The input meter responds to your voice.

If it still does not work

Sound, camera, and devices

Lesson 34 Camera shows a black picture

What the problem means

The camera may be covered, busy, or blocked by permission.

Fix it one step at a time

5. Look for the live picture. What you should see: You can see whether the camera works outside the original app.

Check whether the fix worked

The Camera app displays a live picture.

Sound, camera, and devices

Lesson 35 Bluetooth headphones will not connect

The headphones may be off, connected elsewhere, or not in pairing mode.

3. Click the Windows Start button on the taskbar. What you should see: The Start menu opens.

5. Click Bluetooth & devices. What you should see: The Bluetooth & devices settings appear.

7. Choose Landscape for a standard upright monitor. What you should see: The picture rotates.

8. Click Keep changes only if it looks correct. What you should see: The orientation is saved.

Check whether the fix worked

The screen is upright.

If it still does not work

For a tablet or intentionally rotated monitor, use the orientation matching its physical position.

Display and everyday hardware

Lesson 67 The mouse stops responding

What the problem means

A wireless battery, receiver, or cable problem can prevent movement.

Fix it one step at a time

1. If wireless, turn the mouse off and back on with its own switch. What you should see: Its indicator may light.

2. Replace or recharge its battery if low. What you should see: The mouse has power.

3. If it uses a USB receiver, remove and reconnect that receiver directly to the PC. What you should see: The receiver connection restarts.

4. If wired, reconnect the USB cable or try another PC port. What you should see: You test the wired connection.

5. Move the mouse on a plain surface and test clicking. What you should see: You can check whether it responds.

Check whether the fix worked

The pointer moves and clicks work.

If it still does not work

For Bluetooth mice, check Bluetooth connection. If another mouse works in the same port, the original mouse may need service.

Display and everyday hardware

Lesson 68 The laptop touchpad does not move the pointer

What the problem means

The touchpad may have been disabled by a key or Windows setting.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click the Windows Start button on the taskbar. What you should see: The Start menu opens.

2. Click Settings. If it is not visible, type Settings and click the Settings app in the results. What you should see: The Windows Settings window opens.

3. Click Bluetooth & devices. What you should see: The Bluetooth & devices settings appear.

4. Click Touchpad. What you should see: The Touchpad settings appear.

5. Read the main Touchpad switch. What you should see: You can see whether it is enabled.

6. If off, switch it on. What you should see: Touchpad input is enabled.

7. Move one finger across the touchpad. What you should see: The pointer should move.

8. If a mouse is attached, unplug it briefly and test again. What you should see: You can check whether external-mouse behavior is involved.

Check whether the fix worked

The touchpad controls the pointer.

If it still does not work

If you cannot navigate without a pointer, connect a USB mouse. Some laptops also have a function key marked with a touchpad icon.

Display and everyday hardware

Lesson 69 The number keypad will not type numbers

What the problem means

Num Lock may be off, so keypad keys move the cursor instead.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click Start, type Notepad, and click the matching app in the results. What you should see: Notepad opens.

2. Click inside the blank document. What you should see: The text cursor appears.

3. Press Num Lock once on the keyboard’s numeric keypad. What you should see: Its mode changes; a light may turn on.

4. Type 1, 2, and 3 on the numeric keypad. What you should see: You can check whether digits appear.

5. If they still do not type, test the number row above the letters. What you should see: You can compare the keypad with the main keyboard.

Check whether the fix worked

The keypad types digits.

If it still does not work

Compact laptops may use a function-key combination. Check the keyboard’s labels rather than guessing random shortcuts.

Display and everyday hardware

Lesson 70 A USB accessory works poorly through a hub

What the problem means

An unpowered or faulty hub can cause a device to disconnect.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Save work and stop using the accessory before disconnecting it. What you should see: You avoid interrupting a file transfer.

2. Unplug the accessory from the USB hub. What you should see: It disconnects.

3. Plug it directly into a USB port on the computer. What you should see: Windows detects it directly.

4. Repeat its normal task, such as moving a mouse or testing a webcam. What you should see: You compare operation without the hub.

5. If direct use works, reconnect through another hub port if available. What you should see: You can isolate one bad hub port.

Check whether the fix worked

The device works directly or you identify that the hub causes the symptom.

If it still does not work

For drives, use safe removal before unplugging. A power-hungry accessory may need a powered hub specified by its manufacturer.

Word document problems

Lesson 71 Word will not let you edit a downloaded document

What the problem means

Protected View can intentionally open downloaded documents in a restricted mode.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open the document in desktop Word. What you should see: The document and any warning banner appear.

2. Read the banner at the top. What you should see: You identify Protected View rather than a password lock.

3. Confirm you expected this document and trust its source. What you should see: You can decide whether editing is appropriate.

4. If trusted, click Enable Editing on that banner. What you should see: Word allows editing.

5. Make a small intended edit and press Ctrl and S. What you should see: You can test saving.

Check whether the fix worked

The trusted file can be edited and saved.

If it still does not work

For an unknown file, keep Protected View on. A password-protected or unlicensed document needs a different solution.

Word document problems

Lesson 72 Word opens a document as read only

What the problem means

The file may lack editing permission or be locked by someone else.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Read the message or banner near the top of Word. What you should see: You identify the reason shown.

2. Click File in the upper left. What you should see: The file menu opens.

3. Click Save As, then Browse if available. What you should see: A save location dialog opens.

4. Choose Documents and give the copy a new name. What you should see: You avoid overwriting the original.

5. Click Save, then edit the new copy. What you should see: You can work on a file you control.

Check whether the fix worked

The separate copy can be edited without replacing the original.

If it still does not work

If the original belongs to a shared folder, ask its owner for edit access. Do not bypass someone else’s lock.

Word document problems

Lesson 73 Word changes disappeared after a crash

What the problem means

A recovery copy may exist, but unsaved work is not always recoverable.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open Word again. What you should see: A Document Recovery pane may appear.

2. If recovery files are listed, compare their names and timestamps. What you should see: You can choose the most relevant copy.

3. Open the likely copy and inspect the final paragraphs. What you should see: You check what was preserved.

4. Click File, then Save As. What you should see: You can save a recovered version separately.

5. Choose a clear new filename and click Save. What you should see: The recovery copy is preserved.

Check whether the fix worked

You saved the best available recovery copy.

If it still does not work

If no recovery pane appears, check File, Info, Manage Document, Recover Unsaved Documents if available. Future protection depends on saving regularly and recovery settings.

Word document problems

Lesson 74 Word has an unwanted blank page

What the problem means

Extra empty paragraphs or a manual page break can create a blank page.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Save a copy before changing page structure. What you should see: You can return to the original layout.

2. Click Home on Word’s ribbon. What you should see: Home controls appear.

3. Click the paragraph symbol, called Show or Hide. What you should see: Paragraph marks and manual breaks become visible.

4. Go to the blank page and identify empty paragraph marks or a labeled Page Break. What you should see: You can see what is occupying it.

5. Select only an unnecessary empty mark or manual Page Break and press Delete. What you should see: The extra space may disappear.

6. Check the preceding and following pages. What you should see: You confirm that real content was not removed.

Check whether the fix worked

The extra blank page disappears and nearby content remains intact.

If it still does not work

Do not casually delete a Section Break; it can change layout. A final paragraph after a table may need a smaller font rather than deletion.

Word document problems

Lesson 75 Dots and paragraph symbols appear in Word

What the problem means

Formatting marks are visible; they are editing aids rather than typed content.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click the Home tab. What you should see: Home controls appear.

2. Find the paragraph symbol in the Paragraph group. What you should see: You identify Show or Hide.

3. Click that symbol once. What you should see: Formatting marks toggle off.

4. Open File, then Print to check the preview. What you should see: You can verify the marks are not printed.

Check whether the fix worked

The editing symbols disappear from the normal view.

If it still does not work

If some marks remain, open Word Options, Display and inspect which marks are always shown.

Word document problems

Lesson 76 Pasted text has the wrong font and spacing

What the problem means

Paste may bring formatting from the source into your document.

Fix it one step at a time

1. If you just pasted, press Ctrl and Z once to undo that paste. What you should see: The pasted block is removed.

2. Place the cursor where the text belongs. What you should see: The insertion point is correct.

3. Click Home, then the arrow under Paste. What you should see: Paste choices appear.

4. Choose Keep Text Only when available. What you should see: Text is inserted without the source’s styling.

5. Read the result and reapply intended headings or emphasis. What you should see: You restore meaningful structure.

Check whether the fix worked

The pasted text matches the surrounding document.

If it still does not work

Keep Text Only removes tables and special formatting. Use a copy when testing on a complex document.

Word document problems

Lesson 77 Word text is too tiny to read

What the problem means

Document zoom can change the view without changing the actual font.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open the document in Word. What you should see: Its page appears.

2. Find the zoom slider at the bottom right. What you should see: You can see the current zoom percentage.

3. Click its plus button a few times or move the slider right. What you should see: The view becomes larger.

4. Stop when you can read comfortably. What you should see: The document remains at its actual font size.

Check whether the fix worked

The view is readable without changing the document’s fonts.

If it still does not work

If the printout is tiny too, inspect the actual font size or print scaling instead.

Word document problems

Lesson 78 A paragraph has too much space after it

What the problem means

Paragraph spacing can create gaps even without blank lines.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click within the affected paragraph. What you should see: Word places the cursor there.

2. Click the Layout tab. What you should see: Paragraph spacing controls appear.

3. Find Spacing Before and After. What you should see: You can read the current values.

4. Record those values, then reduce an excessive After value to an appropriate smaller value. What you should see: The gap decreases.

5. Check the adjacent paragraphs before saving. What you should see: You can judge the consistency.

Check whether the fix worked

The unwanted gap is reduced while paragraph text remains intact.

If it still does not work

If spacing is controlled by a style, revise that style consistently rather than adjusting every paragraph separately.

Word document problems

Lesson 79 Word underlines words in the wrong language

What the problem means

The proofing language may not match the text.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Select the affected paragraph by dragging across it. What you should see: That text is highlighted.

2. Click Review on the ribbon. What you should see: Proofing controls appear.

3. Click Language, then Set Proofing Language. What you should see: A language list opens.

4. Choose the language used in that paragraph and click OK. What you should see: Word applies that proofing language.

5. Check the underlined words again. What you should see: The proofing results update.

Check whether the fix worked

Correctly spelled words in the selected language are no longer flagged incorrectly.

If it still does not work

Proper names can still be flagged. Do not turn off all spell checking just to remove a few name warnings.

Word document problems

Lesson 80 Word says Unlicensed Product

What the problem means

Desktop Office may be signed into the wrong account or lack an active license.

Fix it one step at a time

1. In Word, click File. What you should see: The file menu appears.

2. Click Account. What you should see: The signed-in account and product information appear.

3. Read the account email and activation message. What you should see: You can identify a mismatch or expired entitlement.

4. If you own a license under another account, use the sign-in or switch-account option to enter that account. What you should see: Office checks that account’s license.

5. Close and reopen Word when requested. What you should see: You can check whether activation updates.

Check whether the fix worked

Office recognizes your valid license, or you have identified that no active entitlement is present.

If it still does not work

Do not enter a borrowed activation key. If you do not have a license, use an available permitted web editor or another editor for your own files.

Excel worksheet problems

Lesson 81 Excel displays hash marks instead of a number

What the problem means

A column may be too narrow; negative date or time results can also show hash marks.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click the cell displaying hash marks. What you should see: Its full value or formula appears in the formula bar.

2. Locate the column letter above that cell. What you should see: You identify the affected column.

3. Move the pointer to the right boundary of that column heading. What you should see: The pointer becomes a width-adjustment arrow.

4. Double-click that boundary. What you should see: Excel fits the column to its content.

5. Read the cell again. What you should see: You can check whether the value is now visible.

Check whether the fix worked

The value is displayed after widening, or you identify a negative date or time result.

If it still does not work

If widening does not help, inspect the underlying value and number format rather than replacing it blindly.

Excel worksheet problems

Lesson 82 Excel shows formulas instead of results

What the problem means

Show Formulas may be on for the worksheet.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open the affected worksheet. What you should see: Its cells appear.

2. Click the Formulas tab. What you should see: Formula tools appear.

3. Find Show Formulas in the Formula Auditing group. What you should see: You can see its toggle button.

4. If active, click it once. What you should see: Cells display calculated results again.

5. Check two or three formula cells. What you should see: You verify the view changed across the sheet.

Check whether the fix worked

Formula cells show results instead of formula text.

If it still does not work

If only one formula remains as text, check whether that cell is formatted as Text and whether its entry starts with an equals sign.

Excel worksheet problems

Lesson 83 Excel totals do not change after editing

What the problem means

The workbook may be set to manual calculation.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click Formulas on the Excel ribbon. What you should see: Formula controls appear.

2. Click Calculation Options. What you should see: Calculation choices open.

3. Select Automatic. What you should see: Excel recalculates when dependent inputs change.

4. Change one known input in a practice copy. What you should see: You have a controlled test.

5. Check the dependent total and undo the test input if needed. What you should see: You can verify recalculation without altering real records.

Check whether the fix worked

The total updates after a relevant input changes.

If it still does not work

If not, inspect whether the formula references that input. For a large workbook, ask its owner before changing intended manual calculation.

Excel worksheet problems

Lesson 84 Excel ignores numbers in a sum

What the problem means

Some entries may be stored as text rather than numeric values.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click an affected number cell. What you should see: Its value appears in the formula bar.

2. If a green triangle and warning button appear, click the warning button. What you should see: Excel explains the warning.

3. Choose Convert to Number if the warning says Number stored as text. What you should see: The value becomes numeric.

4. Repeat for the relevant selected cells if appropriate. What you should see: Those entries can participate in calculations.

5. Check the SUM total again. What you should see: You can compare the result.

Check whether the fix worked

The intended numeric entries are included in the total.

If it still does not work

Do not convert account numbers, ZIP codes, or identifiers just because they contain digits. If no warning appears, inspect a copy before bulk conversion.

Excel worksheet problems

Lesson 85 Excel shows DIV zero in a formula

What the problem means

The formula is dividing by a zero or empty denominator.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click the cell showing #DIV/0!. What you should see: The formula appears in the formula bar.

2. Read the reference after the division slash. What you should see: You identify the denominator cell or expression.

3. Click that referenced cell and inspect its value. What you should see: You can see whether it is blank or zero.

4. If a valid value is missing, enter the correct source value. What you should see: The denominator is corrected.

5. Return to the formula cell and check the result. What you should see: The formula recalculates.

Check whether the fix worked

The error clears when a legitimate nonzero denominator is present.

If it still does not work

If zero is a valid case, design an explicit zero-case formula in a copy. Do not invent a value just to hide the error.

Excel worksheet problems

Lesson 86 Excel shows a REF error

What the problem means

A formula may refer to cells removed by deleting a row or column.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click the cell showing #REF!. What you should see: The formula bar displays the broken reference.

2. If you just deleted a row or column, press Ctrl and Z once. What you should see: The recent deletion is undone.

3. Check whether the formula result returns. What you should see: You can confirm that deletion caused it.

4. If undo is no longer appropriate, compare the formula with a saved version or neighboring valid formula. What you should see: You identify the intended reference.

5. Correct the reference only when you know which data belongs there. What you should see: The formula points to valid cells.

Check whether the fix worked

The formula refers to the intended data and calculates again.

If it still does not work

Do not copy a nearby formula blindly; its row or column references may differ.

Excel worksheet problems

Lesson 87 Excel shows a NAME error

What the problem means

A function name, named range, or text syntax may be incorrect.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click the cell showing #NAME?. What you should see: Its formula appears in the formula bar.

2. Read the function name immediately after the equals sign. What you should see: You can spot a misspelled function.

3. Compare that name with Excel’s function suggestions while editing a copy. What you should see: Excel shows recognized function names.

4. Correct the spelling or the known missing quotation marks for text. What you should see: The formula syntax changes.

5. Press Enter and check the result. What you should see: Excel evaluates the corrected entry.

Check whether the fix worked

The formula uses recognized names and the error disappears.

If it still does not work

If the formula uses a custom named range, confirm that range exists. An unsupported newer function may require a compatible Excel version.

Excel worksheet problems

Lesson 88 Excel prints a sheet across too many pages

What the problem means

Print scaling or the selected print area may be too broad.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Press Ctrl and P in Excel. What you should see: Print preview opens.

2. Read the page count and look at the preview. What you should see: You can see how the sheet is split.

3. Open the scaling dropdown under Settings. What you should see: Scaling choices appear.

4. Choose Fit All Columns on One Page for a sheet that is too wide. What you should see: The preview fits the width while allowing multiple pages in height.

5. Check whether the text is still readable before printing. What you should see: You can judge whether scaling is practical.

Check whether the fix worked

The preview has the intended width and readable text.

If it still does not work

If text becomes tiny, use landscape orientation or print only the relevant selected range. Avoid forcing a huge sheet onto one page.

Excel worksheet problems

Lesson 89 Excel rows or columns seem missing

What the problem means

Rows or columns may be hidden, or a filter may exclude records.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Look at the row numbers and column letters for gaps. What you should see: You can identify hidden positions.

2. Select the headings on both sides of a gap by dragging across them. What you should see: The neighboring rows or columns are selected.

3. Right-click the selected headings. What you should see: Their context menu opens.

4. Click Unhide if shown. What you should see: Hidden rows or columns become visible.

5. If row numbers are still skipped and a filter is active, use Data, then Clear to clear the filter in a copy. What you should see: Filtered-out rows return.

Check whether the fix worked

The expected rows or columns are visible.

If it still does not work

Clearing a filter changes the view. Confirm with the workbook owner before changing a shared working view.

Excel worksheet problems

Lesson 90 Scrolling in Excel moves the sheet instead of the cell

What the problem means

Scroll Lock can change how the arrow keys behave.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Click a worksheet cell. What you should see: The cell is selected.

2. Press an arrow key and observe whether selection moves or the sheet scrolls. What you should see: You can confirm the symptom.

3. If your keyboard has Scroll Lock, press it once. What you should see: Scroll Lock toggles.

4. If there is no key, click Start, type On-Screen Keyboard, and open it. What you should see: A virtual keyboard appears.

5. Click ScrLk on the virtual keyboard if active. What you should see: Scroll Lock switches off.

6. Return to Excel and press an arrow key. What you should see: The selection should move to the next cell.

Check whether the fix worked

Arrow keys move the selected cell normally.

If it still does not work

If not, check whether you are editing a formula or whether the keyboard itself is malfunctioning.

Gmail and email problems

Lesson 91 An expected email is missing

What the problem means

The message may be in Spam, Trash, another category, or a different account.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open Chrome and type mail.google.com in the top address bar, then press Enter. What you should see: The official Gmail page opens.

2. Sign in to your own account if asked. What you should see: Your mailbox appears.

3. Click your profile picture in the upper right and read the account email. What you should see: You can confirm the correct inbox.

4. Click the search box near the top. What you should see: A search cursor appears.

5. Type in:anywhere followed by a space and the sender’s email address, then press Enter. What you should see: Gmail searches across folders including Spam and Trash.

6. Open a matching message and check its date. What you should see: You can confirm whether it is the expected message.

Check whether the fix worked

You locate the email or confirm it is absent from this account.

If it still does not work

If it never arrived, ask the sender to verify your exact address and check for a bounce message.

Gmail and email problems

Lesson 92 Gmail says storage is full

What the problem means

Google account storage is shared across Gmail, Drive, and Photos.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open Chrome and type mail.google.com in the top address bar, then press Enter. What you should see: The official Gmail page opens.

2. Sign in to your own account if asked. What you should see: Your mailbox appears.

3. Read the storage warning shown in Gmail. What you should see: You confirm the problem is account storage.

4. Click the storage or Manage storage link in that warning. What you should see: The account storage overview opens.

5. Read which service uses the most space. What you should see: You can decide what to review.

6. Download a backup of any important file before deleting it. What you should see: You preserve needed information.

7. Remove only items you have reviewed and no longer need. What you should see: You free space without deleting unknown records.

8. Review Trash before emptying it if permanent deletion is needed for space. What you should see: You understand what would be permanently removed.

Check whether the fix worked

Account storage falls below its limit and mail can resume after the storage update takes effect.

If it still does not work

Storage changes may take time to update. Do not erase your entire mailbox to remove one warning.

Gmail and email problems

Lesson 93 An email comes back undelivered

What the problem means

A bounce message explains why a server rejected or could not deliver mail.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open Chrome and type mail.google.com in the top address bar, then press Enter. What you should see: The official Gmail page opens.

2. Sign in to your own account if asked. What you should see: Your mailbox appears.

3. Open the delivery failure message in the inbox. What you should see: Its error details appear.

4. Find the rejected recipient address and reason. What you should see: You identify the destination and failure.

5. Compare the address with the intended recipient’s confirmed address. What you should see: You can spot a typo.

6. If mistyped, create a corrected message to that confirmed address. What you should see: You can retry the valid destination.

7. If the reason is mailbox full or server unavailable, wait or contact the recipient another way. What you should see: You avoid repeated identical failures.

Check whether the fix worked

The corrected message is delivered, or you identify a recipient-side failure.

If it still does not work

For a blocked message or attachment, read the stated policy. Do not evade a security block by disguising a file.

Gmail and email problems

Lesson 94 An attachment never finishes uploading

What the problem means

The internet connection or file upload may be interrupted.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open Chrome and type mail.google.com in the top address bar, then press Enter. What you should see: The official Gmail page opens.

2. Sign in to your own account if asked. What you should see: Your mailbox appears.

3. Open the saved draft. What you should see: The composition window appears.

4. Look for upload progress or an error beside the attachment. What you should see: You can tell whether it finished.

5. Do not click Send while the attachment is still uploading. What you should see: You avoid sending before completion.

6. Try a familiar website in another tab. What you should see: You test the internet connection.

7. If the upload has failed, remove that failed attachment with its X and attach the trusted file again. What you should see: A new upload begins.

8. Wait until its name appears without progress, then review the message. What you should see: You can confirm upload completion.

Check whether the fix worked

The file is attached and finished uploading before you send.

If it still does not work

If repeatedly failing, check its size and permitted type. Save the draft before restarting the browser.

Gmail and email problems

Lesson 95 You cannot find the attachment in an email

What the problem means

The attachment may be farther down the message or absent from the sender’s email.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open Chrome and type mail.google.com in the top address bar, then press Enter. What you should see: The official Gmail page opens.

2. Sign in to your own account if asked. What you should see: Your mailbox appears.

3. Open the message that should contain the attachment. What you should see: The email body appears.

4. Scroll to the bottom of that individual message. What you should see: Attachment cards usually appear below its text.

5. If the email is a conversation, expand the particular message from the sender. What you should see: Its own attachments become visible.

6. Click the attachment’s download arrow if present. What you should see: The file downloads.

7. Press Ctrl and J to locate the download. What you should see: You can find the saved file.

Check whether the fix worked

You locate and download the intended attachment.

If it still does not work

If no attachment exists, ask the sender to resend it. Do not click an unfamiliar download link merely because it claims to be an attachment.

Gmail and email problems

Lesson 96 Gmail opened the wrong account

What the problem means

Several signed-in Google accounts can make the browser choose another inbox.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open Chrome and type mail.google.com in the top address bar, then press Enter. What you should see: The official Gmail page opens.

2. Sign in to your own account if asked. What you should see: Your mailbox appears.

3. Click the profile picture in the upper right. What you should see: The signed-in account list appears.

4. Read the email address of the current account. What you should see: You identify which mailbox is open.

5. Click the intended account in the list if present. What you should see: Gmail switches to that account.

6. If absent, choose Add another account and sign into your own account. What you should see: The intended mailbox becomes available.

7. Check the profile email again. What you should see: You verify the account switch.

Check whether the fix worked

You are viewing the intended inbox.

If it still does not work

Keep personal and business addresses clearly labeled. Confirm the From address before sending a business message.

Gmail and email problems

Lesson 97 An email was deleted accidentally

What the problem means

Gmail Trash may still contain a deleted message.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open Chrome and type mail.google.com in the top address bar, then press Enter. What you should see: The official Gmail page opens.

2. Sign in to your own account if asked. What you should see: Your mailbox appears.

3. In the left folder list, click More if Trash is hidden. What you should see: Additional folders appear.

4. Click Trash. What you should see: Deleted messages are listed.

5. Find and open the intended message. What you should see: You can inspect its content.

6. Click Move to and choose Inbox. What you should see: The message returns to the inbox.

7. Open Inbox and locate it. What you should see: You verify restoration.

Check whether the fix worked

The message appears in Inbox again.

If it still does not work

Messages already permanently deleted may not be recoverable. Act promptly and check the correct account.

Gmail and email problems

Lesson 98 Gmail appears frozen or shows a temporary error

What the problem means

The browser session or Gmail service may have a temporary problem.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open Chrome and type mail.google.com in the top address bar, then press Enter. What you should see: The official Gmail page opens.

2. Sign in to your own account if asked. What you should see: Your mailbox appears.

3. Read and record the error message. What you should see: You know the exact symptom.

4. Wait briefly, then press Ctrl and R once. What you should see: Gmail reloads.

5. If unchanged, open a familiar unrelated site in another tab. What you should see: You check whether the connection works.

6. Press Ctrl, Shift, and N together and open mail.google.com there. What you should see: You can test Gmail in an Incognito session.

7. Sign in to your account in that window if needed. What you should see: You compare a separate session.

Check whether the fix worked

Gmail loads normally in one session or you identify a broader connection failure.

If it still does not work

If Gmail alone remains unavailable, check its official service status or wait before retrying. Avoid repeatedly deleting browser data.

Gmail and email problems

Lesson 99 A legitimate sender keeps going to Spam

What the problem means

Gmail may have misclassified a message.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Open Chrome and type mail.google.com in the top address bar, then press Enter. What you should see: The official Gmail page opens.

2. Sign in to your own account if asked. What you should see: Your mailbox appears.

3. Click More in the left list if needed, then click Spam. What you should see: Filtered messages appear.

4. Open the message and verify the sender’s actual email address. What you should see: You can check that it is the expected sender.

5. If legitimate, click Report not spam. What you should see: Gmail moves it out of Spam.

6. Check Inbox for that message. What you should see: You verify its new location.

Check whether the fix worked

The legitimate message is restored to the inbox.

If it still does not work

Do not mark a suspicious message safe because it displays a familiar name. The actual address and expected content matter.

Gmail and email problems

Lesson 100 You sent the wrong email and want to stop it

What the problem means

Gmail’s Undo Send control appears only briefly after sending.

Fix it one step at a time

1. Immediately after sending, look at the message confirmation near the lower left of Gmail. What you should see: It may show Message sent with an Undo option.

2. If Undo is still visible, click it immediately. What you should see: Gmail cancels the pending send and reopens the draft.

3. Correct the recipient, attachment, or wording in the draft. What you should see: You can repair the mistake.

4. Read the whole draft again before sending. What you should see: You verify the correction.

Check whether the fix worked

Undo reopens the draft while available; otherwise the message has already left.

If it still does not work

Once Undo disappears, it cannot reliably recall the message. Send a clear correction if needed rather than assuming it was withdrawn.

title: Templar’s Ultimate Dictionary 500 Word Starter Rebuilt
content:
TEMPLAR'S ULTIMATE DICTIONARY

500-WORD STARTER • REBUILT EDITION

Understand the Word. Use the Word. Own the Word.

Built with the Templar Method: Audience + Frequency + Theme + Practical Usage + Word Relationships + Word Upgrade.

How This Starter Is Built

• 500 curated starter headwords chosen to strengthen everyday, academic, professional, technical, creative, and service-based vocabulary.

• Words are connected to the skills you are developing: coding/computers, help desk, Microsoft Office, web design, business/client work, clerical work, research/writing, branding, social media, bookkeeping, career materials, and event planning.

• The 500-word roadmap is the foundation. Developed dictionary entries follow and will continue to be rebuilt under the same system rather than padded with random words.

The 500-Word Vocabulary Roadmap

This is the starter vocabulary set that the full Dictionary and companion Thesaurus will develop. A word may fit more than one field; it is placed under its primary learning theme here.

TEMPLAR’S ULTIMATE THESAURUS

Don’t Just Find Another Word. Find a Better Word.

VOLUME A • EXPANDED EDITION • 105 ENTRIES

A practical personal reference designed to teach meaning, usage, tone, and stronger word choice—not merely list words.

How This Expanded Volume Works

A synonym is not automatically a perfect replacement. Each entry gives you alternatives and reminds you to choose according to exact meaning, strength, formality, and tone.

1. ABANDON

Core Meaning: To leave something or someone completely, or to stop pursuing something.

Synonyms: leave • desert • forsake • relinquish • quit

Antonyms: keep • continue • support

Everyday Choice: Leave

Stronger / More Specific Choices: desert • forsake • relinquish • quit

Choose Carefully: Do not replace “abandon” automatically. Use a synonym only when it preserves the sentence’s exact meaning and tone.

⭐ TEMPLAR’S WORD UPGRADE

Word-choice lesson: If your first thought is “leave,” check whether “abandon” states the idea more precisely: to leave something or someone completely, or to stop pursuing something.

Tone Check: Ask whether you are writing casually, academically, professionally, creatively, or persuasively.
